chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hamza ibn Humran, from Humran ibn A'yan, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from 'Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both).

He said: Salman al-Farisi (may God have mercy on him) said: One day, I was sitting with the Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) when 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) came forward. So he said to him: O 'Ali! Shall I not give you glad tidings? He said: Of course, O Messenger of God.

He said: This is my beloved Gabriel, informing me from God — exalted is His majesty — that He has indeed given your lovers and your Shi'a seven characteristics: gentleness at death, harmony in the solitude [of the grave], light in the darkness [of the grave], security at the fright [of the Resurrection], justice at the Scale, passage over the Path, and entry into Paradise eighty years before the rest of the people of the nations.

key_terms.الرِّفْقَ: Gentleness/ease — relief from the pangs of death
key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Path (Sirat) — the bridge over Hellfire that all must cross
key_terms.الظُّلْمَة: Darkness — the darkness of the grave (barzakh)
key_terms.الْفَزَع: Fright/terror — the great terror of the Day of Resurrection
key_terms.الْمِيزَان: The Scale — the divine balance for weighing deeds on Judgment Day
key_terms.الْوَحْشَة: Loneliness/solitude — referring to the isolation of the grave
key_terms.خِصَال: Characteristics/qualities — virtues or blessings bestowed by God

ai.seo_question: What are the seven characteristics God has given to the lovers and Shi'a of Imam 'Ali according to hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith narrated through Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS), the companion Salman al-Farisi recounts a moment when the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) gave 'Ali ibn Abi Talib glad tidings brought by the angel Gabriel from God. The seven divine gifts promised to those who love 'Ali and follow him (his Shi'a) span from death through the afterlife: ease at the moment of death, companionship in the grave's loneliness, illumination in its darkness, safety on the Day of Resurrection, fair judgment at the divine Scale, safe crossing of the Sirat bridge, and early entry into Paradise by eighty years. This hadith is significant in Shia theology as it directly connects devotion to 'Ali with eschatological rewards, and is narrated by Salman — one of the most esteemed companions in Shia tradition.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Sa`d b. `Abdullah narrated to us from Ya`qub b. Yazid from Muhammad b. Abi `Umayr from Hamza b. Humran from Humran b. A`yan from Abi Hamza al-Thumali from `Ali b. al-Husayn (as).

He said: Salman al-Farisi (rh) said: One day, I was sitting with the Messenger of Allah (s) when `Ali b. Abi Talib (as) came forward. So, he said to him: O `Ali! Shall I not give you glad tidings? He said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah.

He said: My beloved Gabriel informs me from Allah that He has given your lovers and your Shi`a seven characteristics: gentleness at death, harmony in the solitude [of the grave], light in the darkness [of the grave], security at the shock [of the Resurrection], rightly justice at the Scale, a permit on the Path, and entry into Paradise eighty years before the rest of the people of the nations.
